ai.title: Aleph Alpha Releases Kolibri: A 78.1B Open-Weight English-German MoE Model With Only 3.46B Active Parameters
ai.brief: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri , an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language model built for German and English. 4%, per token. 0 license on Hugging Face . The target is sovereign deployment in regulated sectors such as public administration, industry and aerospace. Is it deployable? Yes. The FP8 checkpoint is about 78GB and runs on a single B200, B300 or H200, or on 2 H100 SXM5 GPUs, served through vLLM with dedicated Kolibri reasoning and tool-call parsers. What is Kolibri? Kolibri (Kolibri-1) is a bilingual English-German MoE transformer developed end to end by teams in Germany. According to the technical research report , Aleph Alpha team controlled the full pipeline: data, architecture, training infrastructure, post-training and evaluation. Training ran on infrastructure in Germany and Finland. The design targets the EU General-Purpose AI Code of Practice , the EU AI Act and GDPR.

sec.title: Warlock Ransomware Still Exploits Year-Old SharePoint Flaws to Hit Critical Infrastructure
sec.brief: S. S. S. S. CISA adds Apple Multiple Products flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog Warlock ransomware made headlines back in mid-2025 for exploiting a chain of SharePoint zero-days collectively dubbed ToolShell . More than a year later, the same group is still using that door, and it’s still getting in. Symantec tracks the group behind Warlock as Longlegs, also known as Storm-2603 , and ties it back to older China-nexus clusters called CL-CRI-1040, CamoFei, and ChamelGang. In the past two months alone, Longlegs hit at least four organizations: a water utility, a telecom provider, a regional government body, and a university. All four sit in Portuguese or Spanish speaking countries, spread across Europe, Africa, and Latin America.
